items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: George McCullum, you remember him? Yeah, I remember him. Yeah, I remember him. Yeah, I remember him. Him and his dad both played.

ctx.x: So what about the trumpet players? In the outside, Joe Oliver and Guy Kelly and, let's see, Prince. What about Buddy Petit? Yeah, Buddy Petit. Yeah, Buddy Petit. Yeah, I think Buddy Petit died, you know. Buddy used to get drunk so much, you know. But I always liked his playing. Yeah, Buddy was good, yeah. Yeah. And, let me see, that brother man. George McCullum, you remember him? Yeah, I remember him. Yeah, I remember him. Yeah, I remember him. Him and his dad both played. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.…

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Just a little bands I got him in. ... We should get a little jobs and work together, you know.

ctx.x: Oh, Bud Russel. Russel. Yeah, he, you see, I got to spell it wrong, isn't it? Bud Russel. But he had a band a long time. You remember a boy, don't you, Bud Russel? Bass player. Oh, he had different bands, you know. And he used to get all those youngsters like me, George McCullum. Little young fellas, you know, would play. And we kept him up. He always get a good band. He kept up to, he couldn't play no more, you know. Went to work, things got data on there. He'd get plenty of work through it. How long has he been…
How long has he been dead? How long has he been dead? My brother must be dead about, um.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: Well, they said that George McCullum was his brother.

ctx.x: He's had a brother, Kenia, that's the one. He was a violin player in the Kish Sonson. He'd tell you to play with him three or four pieces. Like hustling and that, send a job down the district. He'd play like that. He'd look like happy, huh? So, um... Very happy. Very happy. Very happy. He died now. He died up in Chicago. He could play with me when I was playing with John Robeser. He used to play with all these bands down there. They were very happy. Alfred Williams, you know him, right? Alfred Williams used to…
